title: Problematic Social Media Use: Results from a Large-Scale Nationally Representative Adolescent Sample
abstract: Despite social media use being one of the most popular activities among adolescents, prevalence estimates among teenage samples of social media (problematic) use are lacking in the field. The present study surveyed a nationally representative Hungarian sample comprising 5,961 adolescents as part of the European School Survey Project on Alcohol and Other Drugs (ESPAD). Using the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS) and based on latent profile analysis, 4.5% of the adolescents belonged to the at-risk group, and reported low self-esteem, high level of depression symptoms, and elevated social media use. Results also demonstrated that BSMAS has appropriate psychometric properties. It is concluded that adolescents at-risk of problematic social media use should be targeted by school-based prevention and intervention programs.

claims.text: 4.5% of Hungarian adolescents in a nationally representative sample were classified as at-risk for problematic social media use based on latent profile analysis.
Adolescents at-risk of problematic social media use report significantly lower self-esteem compared to non-risk and low-risk peers.
Adolescents at-risk of problematic social media use report significantly higher levels of depressive symptoms compared to non-risk and low-risk peers.
Female adolescents report significantly higher weekly time spent on social media than male adolescents.
A cut-off score of 19 on the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale yields 83% sensitivity and 99% specificity for classifying adolescents at-risk of problematic social media use.
The single-factor structure of the Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale demonstrated acceptable structural model fit in adolescent survey data.

limitations.text: Prior research lacks consensual definitions and validated psychometric scales to assess problematic social media use, often relying on platform-specific scales or non-representative samples.
The sample was limited strictly to Hungarian adolescents, limiting direct cross-cultural generalizability.
Data were collected via self-report measures, which are susceptible to memory recall bias, social desirability bias, and extreme response styles.
The study utilized a cross-sectional design, which prevents establishing causal relationships between risk factors and problematic social media use.
Participants may have included non-social networking activities (e.g., gaming or gambling on social platforms) in their subjective conception of social media use while taking the BSMAS.

future_work.text: Conduct cross-cultural studies in different countries to further evaluate the psychometric properties of the BSMAS across diverse adolescent populations.
Apply longitudinal study designs to determine causality and identify contributing developmental factors of problematic social media use.

methodologies.name: BSMAS Latent Profile and Factor Analysis
methodologies.description: Cross-sectional survey of adolescents evaluating BSMAS psychometric properties via Confirmatory Factor Analysis and identifying risk profiles using Latent Profile Analysis.
datasets: European School Survey Project on Alcohol and Other Drugs (ESPAD) Hungary 2015 dataset
conditions: Nationally representative sample of Hungarian adolescents (N = 5,961)
